symptom: `revoke write (Tag_GuestGroup) on entity ModA.Tag from ModA.User` (or the older `revoke ModA.User on ModA.Tag (write (Tag_GuestGroup))`) answered "No access rules found matching …" (later "Unchanged … nothing to revoke"), exited 0, and the association stayed ReadWrite; `write (Label)` on the same rule worked (mendixlabs/mxcli#1225).
cause: execRevokeEntityAccess resolved member names through EntityMembers, which yields attributes only, and fell back to `Module.Entity.Member` for anything else. An association's MemberAccess is stored as `Module.Association` (AssociationQualifiedName), so the ref matched nothing and the backend reported 0 rules modified — indistinguishable from an already-revoked right. GRANT had its own association enumeration (FROM side via ParentID, both ends for OWNER Both, cross-module Both, inherited) that REVOKE never reused.
file: mdl/executor/cmd_security_write.go (accessRuleAssociations shared by grant and revoke; revoke refuses an unmatched member like grant's unmatchedGrantMembers)
insight: Two writers keyed on the same stored reference must share the code that builds it — the grant's association loop and the revoke's attribute-only map had drifted since #758 fixed inherited attributes in both. The idempotent 'nothing to revoke' notice hid it: a count of 0 cannot tell 'already revoked' from 'named something the rule cannot hold'. Separate those before calling the backend — resolve the name, refuse if unknown, and only then let 0 mean unchanged. Measured on a fresh 11.6.6 app: pre-fix binary prints the Unchanged notice and describe still shows write (Tag_GuestGroup); fixed binary revokes it and `mxcli docker check` reports 0 errors.
